doc.title: Tom Baker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Farm childhood, piano lessons and the parade jazz band
summary: No musical family background; he took classical piano from about five and first heard jazz from a band on a truck in Escalon.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: What was it in your childhood that attracted you to being a musician, playing so many instruments and gravitating — Hold on [Phone ringing]
Was there something in your childhood, in your family situation that attracted you to jazz music?

Very late in life. We had a piano in the family. It was my brother, myself and my mother and father. That’s all there was, in a country house, on a farm, in Central California. That gives you the setting. No musical influences at all — there was no bands apart from the high school band. My parents listened to the usual run-of-the-mill, middle-of-the-road Tijuana Brass, Roger Miller, Al Hirt — you know, the usual things that people had in their record collections in those days. Hugo Winterhalter, I remember him.

Mantovani was there, yep, and we had a piano and I was made to take piano lessons, but I really loved playing piano, so I took piano lessons from an early age, classical piano, from about age five for a few years. And after that really got into other things, and in high school took up the trumpet. And I really hadn’t heard any jazz at all, until one day, this was actually a day when there was a parade, and it was called The Fate, in the middle of our little town in California, which was called Escalon. There was a parade going by and I remember there were two bands, they were both on the backs of trucks. And the first one was a rock band, with fairly long hair — it wasn’t that long, but it was pretty long — and they had guitars and an electric bass and a generator on the back. And I remember not liking it very much. And then a bit later on, after the scouts had walked by, there was a jazz band on the truck, with the trombone player sitting on the back.
On the tailgate. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-

Yeah, on the tailgate. And a piano. And I thought wow, this is it. I want to do what they do. And that was my first taste of jazz of any kind. But it really wasn’t until I got to Australia that I started playing any.
